articles.title: Kaliningrad attack closer than expected? NATO’s eastern flank gets sharper teeth with new F-35 jets
articles.description: Poland has received five more F-35A “Husarz” fifth-generation fighter jets, strengthening NATO’s eastern flank amid growing security concerns surrounding Russia and the heavily militarised Kaliningrad exclave. The aircraft landed at the 32nd Tactical Air Base in Łask on August 28, bringing Poland’s delivered F-35 fleet to eight, with more jets expected under Warsaw’s $4.6 billion contract for 32 aircraft. The F-35 programme is part of Poland’s broader military modernisation effort and is intended to replace aging Soviet-era MiG-29 and Su-22 aircraft. With Poland positioned close to Kaliningrad, the arrival of these advanced stealth fighters highlights Warsaw’s preparations for a potentially more dangerous regional security environment.

articles.title: Putin To Meet Trump & Zelensky? CIA Chief Ratcliffe Pushes Three-Way Summit In Moscow | Report
articles.description: A secret CIA mission to Moscow has revealed a dramatic new push to end the Russia-Ukraine war. CIA Director John Ratcliffe reportedly proposed a trilateral summit between Donald Trump, Vladimir Putin and Volodymyr Zelensky during his meetings with Russia's top intelligence chiefs. According to Axios, Ratcliffe also explored whether Moscow's intelligence leadership could help bring Putin back to US-mediated peace talks. The New York Times reported that Ratcliffe delivered a bleak assessment of the war and urged Russia to reach a deal before its position worsens.

articles.title: 'Russophobia Is Taking Over Europe': Fico's Explosive Warning To EU; 'Stop Demonising Russia'
articles.description: Slovak Prime Minister Robert Fico has warned that growing "Russophobia" is pushing the European Union away from its founding ideals as a peace project. Speaking during commemorations of the Slovak National Uprising, Fico urged the EU to pursue diplomacy with Russia instead of further confrontation and military escalation. He argued that Russia should not be "demonised" or isolated from Europe, while criticizing what he described as a growing atmosphere of hostility toward Moscow. Fico's remarks come as divisions within Europe over the Ukraine war continue to widen. Watch this video to know more.
